issues.description: Method addGuestStudents has different parameter lists across artifacts. The template repository declares addGuestStudents with two parameters: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java). The problem statement (task description and UML) specifies a single-parameter method addGuestStudents(int) (problem_statement.md lines 49-51 and 72-73). The solution repository implements the single-parameter signature public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java). This mismatch between the starter code and the specification/reference implementation will confuse students and can cause compilation or test failures when students follow the UML/spec but the provided stub uses a different signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution. Change the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } If input validation is desired, implement it inside that method or provide a separate private/helper method or an overloaded method with a different name so the public API matches the UML and exercise instructions.
